L13: # Blood pressure test
L14: 
L15: A blood pressure test is a simple test to check your blood pressure. High blood pressure can cause serious conditions such as stroke and heart disease.
L16: ## Why a blood pressure test is done
L17: 
L18: A blood pressure test can check if your blood pressure is too high or too low.
L19: 
L20: 【6†High blood pressure (hypertension)】 can cause serious problems like strokes or heart disease, but it does not usually have any symptoms. The only way to find out if you have high blood pressure is to get it checked.
L21: 
L22: 【7†Low blood pressure (hypotension)】 can cause symptoms such as dizziness or fainting.
L23: 
L24: You may be given a blood pressure test:
L25:   * if a doctor thinks you may have high or low blood pressure
L26:   * as part of a general health check
L27:   * to check if high blood pressure is linked to other conditions you may have
L28:   * if you're taking medicine for a long-term condition
L29:   * if you're in hospital to check your health
L30:   * if you're pregnant as part of your antenatal care
L31: 
L32: It's particularly important to get your blood pressure checked if you're at higher risk of high blood pressure, for example if:
L33:   * you're aged 40 or over
L34:   * you're from a Black or South Asian background
L35:   * you have close relatives who have high blood pressure
L36:   * you smoke, drink too much alcohol or caffeine, or eat too much salt
L37:   * you're living with obesity
L38: ## Where to get a blood pressure test
L39: 
L40: You can have your blood pressure checked at:
L41: 
L42:   * most pharmacies
L43:   * your GP surgery
L44:   * some workplaces
L45: 
L46: Some pharmacies may charge for a blood pressure check.
L47: 
L48: Information:
L49: 
L50: ### Free pharmacy checks for over 40s
L51: 
L52: Many pharmacies offer free blood pressure checks for people aged 40 or over.
L53: 
L54: 【8†Find a pharmacy that offers free blood pressure checks】
L55: ## What happens when you have a blood pressure test
L56: 
L57: A blood pressure test usually takes a couple of minutes. You'll be asked to:
L58: 
L59:   1. Sit down and roll up your sleeve, or remove any long-sleeved clothing.
L60:   2. Outstretch your arm, rest it on a table and relax.
L61:   3. Have an inflatable armband (cuff) wrapped around your upper arm.
L62:   4. Stay in that position while the armband fills with air – this may feel uncomfortable for a few seconds until the air releases.
L63: Devices can be different but the armband is usually connected to a small machine that shows your blood pressure measurements.
L64: 
L65: The test may be done a couple of times to make sure the measurement is accurate.
L66: ### Checking your blood pressure at home
L67: 
L68: If a doctor or nurse needs you to check your blood pressure at home, they may give you a blood pressure machine to use. They will show you how to use it.
L69: 
L70: You can also buy your own blood pressure machine to use at home. Machines may be slightly different, so follow the instructions on how to use it to record your blood pressure.
L71: Take your blood pressure, make a note of the numbers, then wait 1 minute before doing it again. You usually do this 2 times, once in the morning and once in the evening. Your doctor or nurse will tell you how many days you need to do this.
L72: If your blood pressure needs to be monitored for 24 hours, you may be given a monitor to wear at home. You'll need to go to a GP surgery, health centre or hospital to have this put on and to return it the next day. Wearing it at home will not affect your daily activities.
L73: 
L74: Information:
L75: ### Find out more on the British Heart Foundation (BHF) website:
L76: 
L77:   * 【9†BHF: How to choose a blood pressure monitor†www.bhf.org.uk】
L78:   * 【10†BHF: Blood pressure chart and diary†www.bhf.org.uk】
L79: ## What your blood pressure result means
L80: 
L81: Blood pressure readings are given as 2 numbers, with the 1st number higher than the 2nd (for example,130/80).
L82: 
L83: The first number measures the systolic pressure. This is the highest level your blood pressure reaches when your heart pumps blood around the body.
L84: 
L85: The second number measures the diastolic pressure. This is the lowest level your blood pressure reaches when your heart relaxes between each heartbeat.
L86: Your blood pressure is usually considered high if it's either:
L87: 
L88:   * 140/90 or higher when checked by a healthcare professional
L89:   * 135/85 or higher when checked at home
L90: 
L91: You can lower high blood pressure by making healthy lifestyle changes, such as eating healthily, exercising regularly and cutting down on alcohol.
L92: 
L93: Many people also need tablets to control their blood pressure. A doctor will recommend the most suitable medicine for you if needed.
L94: 
L95: Information:
L96: ### Blood pressure chart
L97: 
L98: Use our 【11†check your blood pressure reading tool】 to see your reading on a chart and understand what it means.
L99:
